Born: November 14, 1948, 9:14 PM local time, London, England. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating A.

An A rating means the birth time is considered reliable, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be read with confidence. Open King Charles III's chart on Astrolas alongside this read.

Four of the ten planets in this chart sit in the 4th house: the Sun and Mercury in k Scorpio , Venus and Neptune in j Libra . The Astrolas library ties the 4th house to home, family and roots, the part of a chart that holds lineage and inheritance. For a king whose whole public identity rests on an inherited position, that's about as literal as a chart gets.

A second placement complicates the picture. The Moon sits in s Taurus , not in that cluster but in the 10th house of career and public standing, which the library ties to reputation and recognition. The chart reads like a private, family-rooted core pushed, by circumstance, into an unusually public office.

muc.ten: Four planets in the 4th house: Scorpio and Libra
doan: Sun at 22°25' Scorpio, Mercury at 6°57' Scorpio, Venus at 16°23' Libra, and Neptune at 14°08' Libra, all in the 4th house of home and ancestry.

The library's Scorpio Sun is intense and transformative, driven by a need to understand what lies beneath the surface; in the 4th house, that turns toward family, with devotion expressed through small, steady actions rather than declarations, and pride in roots that can run to genealogy or preserving ancestral memory. Mercury in Scorpio thinks the same way, probing rather than skimming; in the 4th house, the library pictures a household where family matters come up first in conversation, in a home that doubles as a study of its own. Venus in Libra is a romantic who values harmony and good manners; in the 4th house, the library reads it as a home decorated with care rather than display, warm ties to relatives, and sometimes an inheritance passed down through the family. Neptune in Libra is generational, a cohort shaped by the founding of the United Nations and the social movements of the 1960s; in the 4th house it becomes personal, an idealized, art-filled image of home as a sanctuary.

Charles's adult identity runs on inherited structure: the Duchy of Cornwall, the estate that funded him as Prince of Wales, and the line of succession itself. He spent decades on the stewardship side of that inheritance, converting Duchy farmland to organic methods and building Poundbury, a town in Dorset designed around traditional architecture rather than modern planning norms. Four planets anchoring home and lineage fit a life spent managing, quite literally, the family estate.

muc.ten: Venus conjunct Neptune, in the 4th house
doan: Venus and Neptune, already together by sign and house, are also in aspect: a conjunction with an orb of 2°15'.

The library reads this pairing as a romantic who idealizes love and leans on imagination, with real potential in the arts, writing, dance or other creative expression, alongside a mysterious, captivating presence. It adds a caution about staying impractical with money or placing trust too easily.

Charles has painted in watercolor for most of his adult life and has sold signed prints of his work for charity. He has also written about design and nature, including a 2010 book on architecture and the environment, and built a public reputation on aesthetic causes most royals left alone, among them classical architecture, organic farming, and the look of the British countryside.

muc.ten: Moon in Taurus, in the 10th house of career
doan: The Moon sits at 0°26' Taurus, in the 10th house of career and public standing.

The library's Taurus Moon is steady and hard to rattle, slow to change its mind, strongest when life feels secure and familiar. In the 10th house, the library ties that steadiness to a need for recognition at work, adding that people with this placement often have a famous or supportive mother and sometimes go into politics or public life, with a career that can include sudden shifts in direction.

Charles's mother, Queen Elizabeth II, reigned for seventy years until her death in September 2022, after which he acceded to the throne. He had already become the longest-serving heir apparent and Prince of Wales in British history by the time that shift arrived, a single, very public change in status after an unusually long, steady wait.

muc.ten: Mars and Jupiter together in Sagittarius, in the 5th house
doan: Mars at 20°57' Sagittarius and Y Jupiter at 29°53' Sagittarius, Jupiter's own sign, both sit in the 5th house of creativity and children.

The library's Sagittarius Mars is bold, impulsive and hungry for adventure, better at starting projects than finishing them, but capable of real results through sheer enthusiasm. Jupiter in Sagittarius, the sign it rules, is read by the library as one of its most fortunate placements, generous, optimistic, drawn to law, philosophy and travel, and willing to walk away from money if it conflicts with belief. In the 5th house, the library adds genuine warmth toward children and young people, often channeled into education or youth projects.

In 1976, Charles used his Royal Navy severance pay to start The Prince's Trust, a charity for disadvantaged young people that has since helped more than a million of them. He has also spoken about environmental issues since the 1970s, long before it was a mainstream concern, often to public mockery at the time.

muc.ten: Saturn in Virgo, in the 2nd house
doan: Saturn sits at 5°16' Virgo, in the 2nd house of money and resources.

The library reads Saturn in Virgo as practical, disciplined and detail-oriented, wanting everything done properly and in order, sometimes to the point of being overly strict about it. In the 2nd house, it describes a serious, careful approach to money, wealth built slowly through patience rather than luck, with a caution against letting frugality turn into real anxiety about scarcity.

Charles has a long-reported reputation for personal thrift, down to reusing worn clothing and disliking waste, and the Duchy of Cornwall under his management became known for disciplined, sustainable farming rather than quick returns.

I Uranus sits at 29°56' Gemini, retrograde, in the 11th house of groups and causes. By sign, Uranus in Gemini marks a whole generation's reform in communication and ideas; the house is where it becomes personal to Charles.

The library's retrograde Uranus in the 11th describes someone who keeps a certain distance from the crowd, connecting deeply with only a few people who share the same thinking, while still caring about group causes and humanitarian work. Ideas tend to form quietly before they're shared, and when they are, they can run ahead of the group's rhythm, sometimes misunderstood at the time even when they hold up later.

Charles's early warnings about plastic waste, intensive farming and the loss of traditional architecture were dismissed for years as eccentric. Decades later, several of the causes he championed alone, among them organic farming, sustainable design and climate change, moved into the mainstream.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: The chart doesn't explain monarchy, and it can't settle whether more than seventy years spent as heir apparent is good fortune or a long wait. What it shows is where the weight sits: four planets anchoring the 4th house of home and lineage, with a Taurus Moon pulled into the 10th house of public life, turning a private, family-rooted chart into a very public one.
